episode.subject: pale pitcher plant
episode.title: The useful edge
episode.body:
I had made the entrance sweet and the way down slippery. A wasp arrived. He put his head inside.

For a while I considered the matter settled.

Then one of his feet tightened on my rim. Another found the edge beside it. He lowered himself farther without giving up either hold. I had attracted an insect who understood the difference between visiting and committing.

There was no correction I could make. I could not turn the rim inward. I could not close the top. All the growing that had brought me to this shape was finished, at least for this particular pitcher. The wasp had found an advantage in the part I had been most pleased with.

He shifted his grip. I prepared to regard that as progress. He shifted it back.

Below him, the whole funnel waited. Above him, his abdomen remained in the sunlight. Between the two he had arranged his legs with an attention to detail I would have admired in almost anyone else.

I had supplied the invitation, the sweetness, the drop. I had also supplied a very good handrail.

proposals.visualReview: A red-brown wasp has its head lowered into a green pitcher while legs visibly brace on the rim. The final physical reversal is visible. Changes of grip, waiting and private certainty are fiction; escape or capture is not claimed.

episode.subject: pale pitcher plant
episode.title: A different part of me
episode.body:
A butterfly settled on my flower. Six feet, almost no weight. I waited for the familiar satisfaction of having caught something.

It stayed. Nothing was caught.

A small gust moved us together, and for once I was pleased that the part it had chosen was good at letting go.

proposals.visualReview: A butterfly rests on the separate yellow-green flower, with another flower behind it. No pitcher trap is mistaken for a blossom. Wind and the narrator’s change of feeling are fiction; pollination or departure is not established.

episode.subject: pale pitcher plant
episode.title: Halfway down
episode.body:
Two ants met inside me and stopped.

I had expected the slope to settle things. They appeared to have found it a convenient place to pause.

One touched the other with an antenna. I waited. My entire interior had become somewhere to exchange news.

proposals.visualReview: Two ants are legible low inside the green veined funnel. The pause and antennal meeting are fictional elaboration, not a verified behavioral sequence. No distressed victim or digestive remains supply the joke.

episode.subject: saguaro cactus
episode.title: Not even an arm yet
episode.body:
The new nub had hardly got clear of my side when it produced a flower.

I spent decades becoming this tall. It has barely become a lump.

There it is, flowering sideways, making the rest of me look as though I have been putting things off.

episode.subject: saguaro cactus
episode.title: The point of arms
episode.body:
A bird landed on one arm. Another took the other side.

For years I had been meaning to do something impressive with all this branching. Now there were feet on the ends of it.

One bird left. I had that arm back to myself.

It was less impressive than I had expected.
